title: The dashboard "stop chain" test requires wsProvider.removeAllListeners() and only checks the stopped set, encoding the registered S1 that stopping a chain also removes the anti-rug subscription, and never checks that buying stops on HTTP-polling chains

evidence.note: case "returns 200 and marks chain stopped" asserts stoppedChains.has("eth") and removeAllListeners toHaveBeenCalled()
stop: stoppedChains.add then ctx.wsProvider.removeAllListeners() with no event (AUD-API-002: also drops the anti-rug log subscription)
only chains.ts and server.ts read stoppedChains: no buy handler consults it (AUD-BUY-011)
the shared fixture wsProvider exposes only removeAllListeners, so no subscription exists for the test to lose

sibling_sites_checked: All cases of chains.test.ts; the unit sibling test/unit/api/chainRestart.test.ts is AUD-TESTU-020. No integration or fork test registers an anti-rug position and then stops/starts its chain.
severity_rationale: S2: the test pins the registered S1 AUD-API-002 as required behaviour and cannot see AUD-BUY-011 (stop does not stop buying).
recommendation: Phase 28: drive stop/start on a context with a real (loopback or scripted) provider carrying both a factory listener and an anti-rug filter; assert the anti-rug filter survives stop and that the HTTP poller and Telegram routing stop buying for the stopped chain (RED today).
affected_cases: POST /api/chains/:name/stop returns 200 and marks chain stopped
escaped_regression: Today: pressing Stop on a chain with open positions removes the anti-rug rug-log subscription (AUD-API-002) and an HTTP-polling chain keeps buying (AUD-BUY-011); the stop test stays green and in fact requires the removeAllListeners call.
